title: A scorecard of every dimension at once, from the record alone: throughput, lead time, first-pass quality, rework, autonomy, reliability, cost and gate time, with n, direction and trend
prompt:
Read the control stream and its fold in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_control_apply`: every record type, `task.assigned` with `created_by` and `objective`, `task.delivered`, `task.reviewed`, `task.gated` and its verdicts, `task.landed`, `task.cancelled`, `mission.halted`, `mission.resumed`; `spawn_control_refold`); the `spawn_commands` table (`principal`, `idempotency_key`, `state`, `succeeded`, `error`, `created_at_ms`, `finished_at_ms`, `action.tags`); in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs the delivery keys (`deliver-<task>-<revision>` and `-retry-<n>`), `attempts()` (when a delivery's retries are spent: `DELIVERY_RETRIES`, `NOT_READY_FREE`, `PANE_NOT_READY`, `MAY_HAVE_TYPED`) and the digest tags (`Escalation::tag` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs, `stall-<task>-<step>-<n>` in dispatch/stall.rs); the transcript archive in crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs (`<workspace root>/.transcripts/<agent>/<native>.jsonl`, copies `<native>.<n>.jsonl`) and a real archived transcript (an assistant message is split over several lines, one per content block, each repeating `message.id`, `message.model` and `message.usage`); the gate's stage line (`| stage gate <result> <ms>ms total`, scripts/stage.sh and scripts/rsi/gate.sh); crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (the commands), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (the `/api/*` routes, the reader login) and web/src (App.tsx, the views under components/); docs/design.md §14 and docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.

The problem. The owner's goal (2026-11-06) is a Spawn that is excellent on every dimension at once, on the Pareto frontier: no dimension improves by letting another regress. Nothing measures the dimensions. How fast the fleet lands work, how often work is sent back, how often a person had to step in, how often the machinery failed, what it cost and how long the gate takes are each in the record (the event log, the mission records, the command rows, the archived transcripts), but nobody can read them without a day of SQL, so no change can show it moved one dimension without hurting another.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. The command. `spawn scorecard [--mission N] [--since <time>] [--until <time>] [--json]`. `<time>` is RFC 3339 (`2026-10-02T00:00:00Z`) or a span back from now (`36h`, `7d`); `--since` defaults to `7d`, `--until` to now (the database's clock, `spawn_now_ms()`). The window is [since, until); the previous window is the same length just before it. Without `--mission`: the fleet, then every mission that has a task assigned before `until` and open, landed or with any counted record in either window, by id. With `--mission N`: that mission alone. Computed only from the record: the control events of session_control (their `recorded_at_ms`), the `spawn_commands` rows and the archived transcripts under `$SPAWN_WORKSPACE_ROOT/.transcripts` (or `--root`). No new hand-kept counter, table or column: a reader of the same record gets the same numbers, and the same flags give byte-identical JSON (no field depends on when it was asked once `--until` is given).
2. Definitions (state each in a new section of docs/design.md, as written here). Times are a record's `recorded_at_ms`; an event belongs to a window or day when since <= t < until. Days are UTC dates; `days` lists every UTC day the window covers, oldest first, each computed as a window of its own (clipped to the window). A task is *landed* at its `task.landed`, or, on a mission without a gate, at its `task.reviewed` with `accepted` true; it is *closed* at its landing or its `task.cancelled`; it is *open* from its `task.assigned` until it is closed (or until the window's end). A task's mission is its `mission_id`. A command belongs to the mission of the task its key names (`deliver-<task>-...`), else of the task open on its session when it was created, else to the fleet only.
- throughput: landings in the window divided by the open hours, where the open hours are the length of the union of the scope's open-task intervals clipped to the window. Higher is better. Parts: `landed`, `open_hours`.
- lead time: for each landing in the window, its landing time minus its assignment time; for a task with an objective, the assignment of the earliest task of the same mission and objective that was cancelled at or before this task's assignment (the objective's first try, so a re-issue does not hide the wait). `value` is the median, `p90` the 90th percentile, both by nearest rank (the value at rank ceil(p/100 x n) of the sorted list), in whole ms. Lower is better.
- first-pass quality: the share of the window's landings whose task never had a send-back. Higher is better. Part: `first_pass`.
- rework: send-backs in the window per landing in the window. A send-back is a `task.gated` with verdict `rejected`, `conflict` or `incompatible`, or a `task.reviewed` with `accepted` false. Lower is better. Parts: `send_backs`, `by_verdict` {`rejected`, `conflict`, `incompatible`, `reviewed`}.
- autonomy: owner interventions in the window per landing. An intervention is (a) a command whose principal is `human` or `spawn` (the board's and the CLI's: Spawn's loops have principals of their own), at its creation; (b) a `mission.resumed` (only a human resumes); (c) an owner task: a `task.assigned` with `created_by` `human` on a mission whose `accept` is `review`; (d) a cancel-and-reassign: a `task.cancelled` whose `by` is absent or `human`, followed in its mission by a `task.assigned` for the same objective (or, without one, the same brief), counted at that assignment. A cancellation by one of Spawn's loops (`by` `spawn-dispatch`, objective 019) is not an intervention. Lower is better. Parts: `interventions`, `by_kind` {`command`, `resume`, `owner_task`, `cancel_reassign`}.
- reliability: failures of the machinery in the window per landing: every command finished with `succeeded` false (at its creation); every spent delivery, judged as deliver.rs `attempts()` judges it (no attempt succeeded, none open, none `MAY_HAVE_TYPED`, more than `DELIVERY_RETRIES` failures past the first `NOT_READY_FREE` refusals for a pane not ready), at its last attempt's finish; every stall, a distinct `stall-<task>-<step>-<n>` tag in a `spawn-dispatch` input's `tags`, counted once whatever the number of digests that carried it, at the first; and every infrastructure gate outcome, a `task.gated` with verdict `aborted`, `no_room` or `host_fault` (objective 020). Lower is better. Parts: `events`, `by_kind` {`failed_command`, `spent_delivery`, `stall`, `gate_infrastructure`}.
- cost: model tokens in the window per landing. A transcript's assistant line with a `message.usage` counts once per (agent, `message.id`), across every copy file, at its `timestamp`: input + cache creation + cache read + output tokens, under its `message.model`. A mission's tokens are those of its tasks' agents between each task's first `task.delivered` and its close (the window's end when open); the fleet's are every agent's, the supervisor's included. Also the gate's machine time: the sum of the gate runs' wall clock in the window (below). Lower is better. Parts: `tokens`, `by_model` {<model>: {`tokens`, `per_landed`}}, `gate_ms`, `gate_ms_per_landed`.
- gate time: the median (nearest rank) wall clock of the gate runs in the window, in ms. A gate run is a `task.gated` whose record names its wall clock: its `gate_ms` when present, else the last `| stage gate <result> <ms>ms total` line of its `log`; a record with neither ran no measured gate and is not counted. Lower is better. Part: `runs`.
3. The answer. Every dimension, for every scope and every day, is an object with `value`, `n`, `enough`, `better` (`higher` or `lower`), `previous`, `trend` and its parts. `n` is the number of landings (the number of gate runs for gate time). The minimum n is 3 (`min_n` in the JSON): below it `value` and every per-landing part are null, `enough` is false, and the text form says `not enough data` (with n and the minimum) instead of a number. `previous` is the value over the previous window (null when not enough there); `trend` is `better`, `worse` or `same` by the dimension's direction, comparing the rounded values, null when either is null; days carry `previous` and `trend` null. Ratios are rounded to 3 decimals (half away from zero); ms and token counts are whole numbers. The JSON is `{since_ms, until_ms, previous_since_ms, min_n, scopes: [{scope: "fleet"|"mission", mission: null|id, dimensions: {throughput, lead_time, first_pass, rework, autonomy, reliability, cost, gate_time}, days: [{day: "YYYY-MM-DD", dimensions: {...}}]}]}`; a part is always present (null when it has no value), never left out. The text form (without `--json`) shows the same numbers, one line per dimension, with the direction and the trend.
4. The dashboard. A read-only Scorecard view in web/src shows the same numbers (fleet and missions, the window and its days, `not enough data` where the JSON says so, the direction and the trend), from a new `GET /api/scorecard?mission=&since=&until=` that answers exactly the JSON of `spawn scorecard --json` with the same flags. Serve reads as its reader login (grant it what it needs, read-only) and reads transcripts from its own SPAWN_WORKSPACE_ROOT.
5. Records that make the measures exact from now on. `task.cancelled` names `by` (the caller: `human`, `spawn_supervisor`, or the loop), so (d) can tell a person's cancellation from Spawn's; older records without it count as a person's. Nothing is backfilled.
6. Causality (§14): every number is read from a record that names what it covers (a record's time, a command's key and session, a transcript line's message id); nothing is inferred from absence or from the order loops ran in. Say so in the module comment.
Add unit tests for every definition (each dimension on a small history, the minimum n, nearest-rank percentiles, the open-hours union, the re-issue lead time, the token de-duplication across lines and copies, the attribution of commands to missions, a stall tag sent twice, rounding and trends), and in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/ for the queries.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/017.sh (read it: its header lists the seeded history and the hand-worked numbers). It seeds a fresh database with a known history and no loop: control records written straight into spawn_events with chosen times and folded by `spawn_control_refold()`, command rows, and archived transcripts. Two missions over a 48-hour window and the 48 hours before it: twelve tasks, landings on a gated and on a review mission, a rejection, a conflict, a review send-back, a spent delivery cancelled and re-issued, a pane refusal, an abort, a no_room, a halt and a resume, a stall digest sent twice, human and CLI commands, owner tasks, and transcripts with split and copied messages and lines outside the window. It checks:
- (1) `spawn scorecard --since 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z --until 2026-10-04T00:00:00Z --json` answers, with `min_n` 3, the window's bounds and the scopes fleet, mission 1, mission 2;
- (2) every value, n, enough, better, previous, trend and part of the eight dimensions, exactly, for the fleet and each mission over the window and for the fleet's two days (e.g. fleet throughput 0.171 over 35 open hours, lead time median 18000000 and p90 28800000 ms, autonomy 1.167 from 7 interventions, reliability 1.667 from 10 events, cost 2670 tokens per landing, gate time 600000 ms, better than 900000; mission 2's two landings `not enough data`);
- (3) `--mission 2` gives mission 2 alone, and its text form says `not enough data`;
- (4) `GET /api/scorecard` on `spawn serve` answers the same JSON as the CLI.
On the live main (06cc205; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "`spawn scorecard --since 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z --until 2026-10-04T00:00:00Z --json` exited 1: spawn: unknown command scorecard". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
